item.title: Two held after €310,000 drugs seizure in Limerick and Cork
item.description: Two people are still being held after drugs worth over 310 thousand euro were seized in Limerick and Cork. The discoveries were made in Bruree and Charleville. The first seizure of drugs was made when a home was searched in Bruree in County Limerick on Friday evening. item.title: Extra care urged on roads amid Status Yellow ice warnings
item.description: People are advised to take extra care on the roads and look after elderly neighbours during the current spell of icy weather. The north and west of the country are worst hit, with snow forecast in places. Status yellow ice warnings will remain in effect for the entire country until 11 o'clock this morning and return again at 6 o'clock this evening. Advertisement Alan O’Reilly from Carlow Weather says the wintry weather is set to continue for a few days yet.

item.title: Man dies after serious assault in Roscommon
item.description: A man has died following a serious assault in County Roscommon. It happened on Barrack Street in Ballaghaderreen at around 1am on New Year's Day. A man in his 30s was taken to Beaumont Hospital in a critical condition - Gardaí have this morning confirmed he has since passed away. Advertisement A man in his 40s has been charged in connection with the investigation. He is due to appear before Roscommon District Court this morning. Gardaí say investigations are ongoing.

item.title: Local senator praises first aid volunteers
item.description: A local senator says that as community and as a country we are deeply indebted to those who volunteer as first aid responders. Robbie Gallagher noted that the defibrillators can be seen everywhere, and that it's a huge credit to the local community to have those installed. He was speaking as he has recently been approached by the Irish Heart Foundation and has been raising the importance of introducing CPR and first aid training as part of the driver theory test. item.title: Weather warnings extended across region
item.description: Weather warnings have been extended across the Northern Sound region, with temperatures set to barely rise above zero today. A low of minus 6 point 8 degrees was recorded overnight, and snow has fallen in parts of the north-west. A status yellow snow-ice alert for Cavan, Monaghan, Donegal, Louth and all of Connacht will remain in place until 11 o'clock tomorrow morning. This year junior infants in Cavan and Monaghan benefitted from the My Little Library Initiative. item.title: Live Updates: St. Brigids v Scotstown
item.description: Follow live updates of the All-Ireland club football semi-final as St. Brigid's face Scotstown. Connacht champions Brigid's were All-Ireland champions in 2013 and runners up in 2024. Whereas, Ulster champions Scotstown are back at this stage for the first time since 1989. Throw-in at Kingspan Breffni is 3pm. Advertisement

item.title: Brendan Smith welcomes Dundalk IT and Queen’s University partnership
item.description: Fianna Fáil TD for Cavan Monaghan, Brendan Smith, has welcomed the announcement that Dundalk IT and Queen's University have entered into an agreement to advance a Partnership whereby Dundalk IT would become University College of Queens, Belfast. Deputy Smith described the news as a welcome development for the North East including Cavan and Monaghan. According to the local TD, the existing linkages between Cavan and Dundalk will prove very beneficial for many students for the future. Advertisemen
